title: Tokyo Ghoul
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In an alternate Tokyo, ghouls who look human but must eat human flesh live in secret. University student Ken Kaneki survives a ghoul attack and is surgically turned into a half-ghoul, then learns to survive among ghouls at the cafe Anteiku while hiding his condition from his human friends. The story follows his struggle to keep his humanity amid conflict with the ghoul-hunting CCG.
life_message: It holds up keeping one's humanity and care for others when the world forces a choice between two hostile sides.

delivery.evidence: ANN's vol. 1 review calls one book-within-the-book analogy a bit heavy-handed but finds the humanity question carried by Kaneki's situation.

personified.ideology: keeping one's humanity between two hostile sides

delivery.note: Its question about humanity is carried mainly by Kaneki's position between ghouls and humans, with one pointed literary analogy.

winners_losers: Neither ghouls nor ghoul hunters win cleanly; those caught between the two groups suffer most. Sympathy goes to outsiders who try to bridge both worlds.
